stories.headline: Fantasy basketball: Points league draft tiers
stories.summary: André Snellings groups players into tiers by each position for points leagues.
stories.body:
In our recent 10-team points mock draft, the first round leaned heavily toward point guards and big men. Four point guards came off the board, along with three power forwards and two centers. Anthony Edwards was the only shooting guard selected, and no small forwards were taken. The first small forward didn't go until Amen Thompson at No. 13 overall, followed by Scottie Barnes and Cooper Flagg later in the second round.

By the middle of the draft, the board looked much different. Round 6 alone featured four small forwards: Caleb Wilson, Brandon Miller, Franz Wagner and Trey Murphy III. That tells you a lot about this year's player pool. Point guards and big men are prominent near the top, while much of the wing depth shows up later. That doesn't mean you have to force a small forward early, but you should know where each position starts to thin out.

Point guard gives you more room to wait. My third tier alone includes Tyrese Maxey, Jalen Brunson, Trae Young, Josh Giddey, Devin Booker, Tyrese Haliburton, James Harden, LaMelo Ball and Jamal Murray. If several of those players are still available, there may be no reason to reach for the position.

Small forward is different. The position has useful depth later, but the top options disappear quickly. Power forward also has a large middle group, while center is more concentrated near the top, with Nikola Jokic in his own tier and Victor Wembanyama right behind him.

This is where the board starts to matter more than the rankings. A straight ranking tells you who I value more. Tiers tell you where the drop-offs are. If several point guards remain in the same tier but only one small forward is left before a drop, that should factor into your pick. The same applies when a position has enough depth to let you wait another round.

The tiers below are based on our preseason projections and show where we see the biggest breaks at each position. The idea is simple: know where you can wait and where waiting too long could cost you.

Point guard

Thoughts on PGs:

Gilgeous-Alexander is projected for 31.3 PPG, 6.4 APG and 1.7 SPG, while Doncic is projected for 33.0 PPG, 8.9 APG and 8.5 RPG. Gilgeous-Alexander has the stronger durability track record, while Doncic brings elite production across points, rebounds and assists.
Cunningham stands alone in Tier 2. He finished sixth in fantasy points per game last season and is projected for 24.6 PPG and 9.8 APG.
The depth starts in Tier 3 with Maxey, Brunson, Young, Giddey, Booker and Haliburton. Haliburton could outperform this group if he returns to form after missing last season.
Harden, Ball and Murray make up Tier 4 and give managers another strong group if they wait at the position. Ball brings plenty of upside in Minnesota, while Harden and Murray remain reliable fantasy options.
There are also a few younger guards worth watching later, including Harper and Acuff Jr.
Point guard is deep enough that managers who miss the top two tiers should still have plenty of options later in the draft.

Shooting guard

Thoughts on SGs:

Edwards remains the top shooting guard and is projected for 30.3 PPG after setting career highs in scoring and field goal percentage last season. LaMelo Ball's arrival could help Edwards get cleaner looks without changing his role as Minnesota's primary scorer.
Mitchell is close behind him in the projections. Harden could lower some of his shot volume, but his playmaking should also create easier scoring chances.
White, Reaves and Bane make up Tier 2. White brings strong all-around production, Reaves is now the clear No. 2 option behind Doncic, and Bane remains one of the safer scoring options at the position.
Alexander-Walker, Daniels and Murray form Tier 3. They offer different paths to production, with Daniels standing out for his all-around contributions.
Edgecombe shined as a rookie but has a crowded roster with the 76ers in Year 2, while the promising Peterson is another later-round name to watch.
There is enough depth at shooting guard that managers who miss the top tier should still be able to find value in the middle rounds.

Small forward

Thoughts on SFs:

Barnes, Thompson and Flagg make up Tier 1 and give the position three high-end options near the top of the projections. Barnes and Thompson bring more all-around production, while Flagg has a chance to take another step in Year 2.
Irving's return should allow Flagg to play more often in a role that fits his game after Dallas used him at point guard at times last season.
Avdija and Leonard make up Tier 2. Avdija is coming off career highs in scoring and assists, while Leonard still produces at a high level when healthy.
Tier 3 is where the depth of the position stands out. Knueppel, Brown, LeBron James, Bridges and Michael Porter Jr. give managers several starting-caliber options without having to reach earlier.
Wilson and Dybantsa are two rookies worth targeting later. Wilson is projected for 17.9 PPG and 8.1 RPG, while Dybantsa is projected for 20.1 PPG and could lead the rookie class in scoring.
Small forward still has enough depth in the middle tiers that managers don't have to force the position early.

Power forward

Thoughts on PFs:

Antetokounmpo and Johnson make up Tier 1. Giannis is projected for 32.1 PPG, 11.4 RPG and 6.3 APG in his first season with Miami, while Johnson is coming off 22.5 PPG, 10.3 RPG and 7.9 APG after becoming the centerpiece of Atlanta's offense.
Tatum stands alone in Tier 2 and gives managers another reliable high-end option before the position opens up in the next group.
Durant and Siakam make up Tier 3. Durant remains one of the league's top scorers, while Haliburton's return should help Siakam get easier looks.
Williams and Mobley make up Tier 4 and are close enough in the projections that managers should not need to reach.
Tier 5 includes Banchero, Randle, Markkanen and Williamson. Randle should have a larger role in Brooklyn, while Williamson still has plenty of upside when healthy. New Orleans' crowded frontcourt could make his role less predictable.
Boozer is the rookie to watch. He is projected for 18.5 PPG and 7.9 RPG and should have a major role right away in Memphis.
Power forward still has useful depth. If you miss Giannis, Johnson or Tatum, there are several options available in the next few tiers.

Center

Thoughts on Cs:

Jokic gets his own tier. He has led fantasy basketball in points for six straight seasons and is projected for 28.3 PPG, 12.7 RPG and 10.1 APG. He remains ahead of the rest of the position.
Wembanyama stands alone in Tier 2. He is projected for 26.3 PPG, 12.2 RPG and 3.5 BPG and has the per-game production to challenge Jokic. The concern is availability after he missed 54 games over the last two seasons.
Sabonis stands alone in Tier 3 after averaging roughly 19 points, 13 rebounds and 7 assists per game over his previous three full seasons.
Sengun and Towns make up Tier 4, while Duren, Davis and Adebayo form Tier 5. Duren is coming off a big jump in production at age 22, while Davis could outperform this group if he stays healthy.
Allen, Reid and Okongwu make up Tier 6 and give managers another group of reliable options before the position opens up. Tier 7 has several players with similar projected value but very different profiles. Clingan, Kessler, Gobert, Holmgren, Embiid, Sarr, Zubac and Jackson all bring different combinations of upside, role security and injury risk.
Kessler is expected to be healthy after shoulder surgery limited him to five games last season, and his move to the Lakers should put him in a favorable spot next to Doncic.
Embiid has a much higher per-game ceiling than the rest of Tier 7, but his availability makes him harder to trust.
Ware is another later-round name to watch. He averaged nearly a double-double in roughly 22 MPG last season and could take on a larger role in Milwaukee.

Final thoughts
Managers don't need to force many positions early. Point guard and shooting guard are deep, while small forward and power forward offer more options than they did last year. Center is different at the top, with Jokic, Wembanyama and Sabonis each occupying their own tier before the position opens up. That is where tiers help. Pay attention to where the drop-offs are and where you can afford to wait.

stories.headline: Steelers receiver Michael Pittman aggravates foot, out weeks
stories.summary: Steelers receiver Michael Pittman Jr. aggravated a foot injury and is out multiple weeks.
stories.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Steelers wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. aggravated a foot injury in Wednesday's practice, and he will likely be sidelined multiple weeks, coach Mike McCarthy said Thursday.

Pittman had been dealing with plantar fasciitis in his left foot, which led him to miss the Week 2 game against the New England Patriots. The receiver was spotted using a scooter to keep weight off his left foot in the locker room following Wednesday's practice.

"It's the same foot, so it's going to be a multiple-week injury," McCarthy said. "We're still going through the evaluation of his roster position."

The Steelers landed the veteran Indianapolis Colts receiver for a late-round pick swap in a March trade and subsequently signed him to a three-year, $59 million extension. The 2020 second-round pick was productive and versatile in six seasons with the Colts, posting two 1,000-yard seasons. Pittman, though, hasn't been productive early on in his tenure in Pittsburgh, catching just seven passes on 12 targets for 89 yards. The 29-year-old also missed a large chunk of training camp with a separate, undisclosed injury.

Pittman's injury comes as the Steelers prepare to face his former team Sunday -- an occasion that quarterback Aaron Rodgers pointed out in his Wednesday news conference.

"We'd love to get Pitt involved, especially this week, being his former team, but there's going to be opportunities for a lot of guys," Rodgers said.

That rings especially true with McCarthy's assertion that Pittman will miss multiple weeks. Without Pittman, the Steelers will lean more heavily on third-year receiver Roman Wilson and rookie Germie Bernard. Wilson, who was largely uninvolved in the offense during his first two seasons, has become one of Rodgers' go-to targets. He caught touchdown passes in Weeks 3 and 4, marking the first time in his career that he recorded touchdown receptions in consecutive games. Wilson, a 2024 third-round pick, has 14 receptions on 24 targets for 188 yards and is averaging 13.4 yards per reception as a field-stretching target.

"Roman has a second gear that you love to utilize as much as you possibly can," McCarthy said Thursday, adding that Wilson has improved his route-running.

Bernard, a second-round pick out of Alabama, has seven receptions on 11 targets, including eight against the Patriots, for 60 yards.

"Germ has been balling since he first got here," wide receiver DK Metcalf said. "Big kudos to him and his preparation, because like I told him, it's very difficult trying to learn the signals and the offense as well. He's done a hell of a job."

While the Steelers' offense will be down at least one player -- and possibly more with Rico Dowdle continuing to miss practice after twice dislocating a toe in the loss to New England -- the defense could soon be getting a boost. The Steelers opened the 21-day practice window for DeShon Elliott to return from injured reserve. Elliott, a physical and hard-hitting safety, sustained a season-ending knee injury in Week 8 of the 2025 season. While he participated in training camp and played in a preseason game, Elliott was placed on injured reserve after the Steelers ultimately decided he needed more time before playing in the regular season.

McCarthy also said he saw encouraging signs from starting cornerback Jamel Dean, who exited the Thursday night loss to the Browns with an ankle injury. McCarthy said Dean told the athletic training staff he felt better than expected on Monday. Even so, the cornerback didn't participate in Wednesday's practice.

To supplement the waning cornerback depth, the Steelers signed Sean Murphy-Bunting off the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' practice squad and Terell Smith off the Washington Commanders' practice squad.

stories.headline: Erling Haaland calls on Man City to 'stay positive' amid Premier League charges case
stories.summary: Erling Haaland has said that everyone at Manchester City has to "stay positive" as the team prepares to play their first matches since being found guilty of breaching Premier League regulations.
stories.body:
Erling Haaland has said that everyone at Manchester City has to "stick together" and "stay positive" as the team prepares to play its first match since being found guilty on 100-plus charges of serious breaches of Premier League financial regulations.

Most City players were away representing their respective countries during the extended international break when the outcome of City's legal battle against the Premier League was made public.

City have branded the verdict "unsafe" and have lodged a "comprehensive appeal" of the independent commission verdict.

- What's next for Man City? Appeals, possible punishments, how long it could take

Enzo Maresca's team travels to face Liverpool on Sunday and seems certain to receive a hostile reception from the Anfield crowd.

"I think they [the City fans travelling to Anfield] are going to have a good time," Haaland told club media.

"We have to stick together. We have to stay with each other, and we have to stay positive.

"No matter what happens in life, we always have to have a smile. We have to stay positive, look ahead and try to win football games and try to enjoy the situation and win the game."

Haaland joined City from Borussia Dortmund in 2022 and has won a host of individual and team honors in the years since.

"I care a lot about this place -- the UK, generally," he said. "My mother as well [as my father], they lived here for 10 years -- they lived in Nottingham and Leeds.

"They never lived in Manchester, but obviously my father trained over at Carrington every day.

"I spent my first four years here, my brother nine and my sister six, so it's a special place for us.

"I care a lot about City, I have to say.

"I care a lot about the fans because I'm a fan myself -- I feel with them as well."

- Sources: Guardiola set to attend first City home game since guilty verdict

The Norway international added in an interview with Sky Sports: "And no matter what happens in life, we always have to have a smile.

"So we have to stay positive, look ahead and then try to win football games and then try to enjoy the situation and the game."

Information from PA contributed to this story.

stories.headline: Harry Kane interest in MLS 'fulfilment of a dream' - commissioner
stories.summary: MLS commissioner Don Garber would love Harry Kane to follow Lionel Messi across the pond and says the England skipper's interest helps fulfil a dream that Sir David Beckham kept alive.
stories.body:
MLS commissioner Don Garber would love Harry Kane to follow Lionel Messi across the pond and says the England skipper's interest helps fulfil a dream that Sir David Beckham kept alive.

The 33-year-old is in the running for the Ballon d'Or having scored 73 goals for club and country in a season that saw the striker win the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich before World Cup bronze.

Kane shows no signs of slowing and he marked his record-equalling 125th England appearance by extending his international goal tally to 91 in Tuesday's 3-0 Nations League win against Czechia.

The striker scored six goals across a four-match camp that began with him revealing his interest in eventually moving to MLS as the striker spoke about his dreams of being an NFL kicker.

"I'd love for him to do that," commissioner Garber said. "I think, for me, it is the fulfilment of the dream that we had to build a proper soccer league that would drive a soccer nation. That sounds colloquial but actually we have that written down.

"We wanted to create something that would have the Harry Kanes of the world say 'I'd kind of like to play in MLS.' And I think Messi proved that.

"That was a competitive process, working to ensure that we had a dynamic that would be better than going back to Barca, working a dynamic that would not have him want to play in Saudi Arabia.

"Play in Miami, have them be able to build a new stadium and have him set records and be an MVP, and then have an unbelievable goodbye [this week] from his international career."

Garber welcomes Kane's keenness to move to MLS and is eternally grateful to another England captain as he prepares to step down from the post of commissioner he has held since 1999.

Beckham's move to LA Galaxy acted as the catalyst for the league's growth, which only accelerated when the former midfielder helped form Inter Miami and sign Argentina great Messi in 2023.

"I don't think I would say one is more important than the other," Garber said of the star duo's impact.

"David put this league on the path to credibility and respect. In the prime of his career, he came to LA.

"He came into Major League Soccer and showed the world that this league can be competitive, it could be respected, it could be fun, it could have great players.

"It attracted [Thierry] Henry and many, many other players right after that, so without David there's probably no Major League Soccer.

"That being said, Major League Soccer would not be the global phenomenon and not be sort of on the hearts and minds of just about anybody in the world without Leo Messi."

Garber will become chairman at the turn of the year and is proud of his legacy with MLS, which was founded as part of the bid to hold the 1994 World Cup in a country that has just co-hosted the largest edition of the tournament.

- Harry Kane is England's greatest ever player - Jude Bellingham

- Harry Kane's England milestones: From his first cap to becoming all-time record goalscorer

- England Nations League takeaways: Kane makes history, Tuchel steadies ship

The 68-year-old says they have made the planet's "biggest commercial market for the sport" during that time and is excited to see how they build on firm foundations.

"We just went from a country road, now we're getting onto the highway," Garber told the Press Association. "And we've got to get better.

"We have to have a league that is more competitive, that has an ability to get into the Club World Cup and win games. Miami won one.

"Not just be there but have people think that an MLS team can compete against other clubs in the world."

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: With an 84-point lead in the drivers' standings, it is looking increasingly likely that Kimi Antonelli will be crowned F1's youngest world champion in the next two months.
stories.body:
With an 84-point lead in the drivers' standings, it is looking increasingly likely that Kimi Antonelli will be crowned F1's youngest world champion in the next two months.

Determining when and where that coronation will likely take place is much harder to say, not least because there are still question marks over how many races remain in the F1 calendar.

Antonelli's closest competitor, Mercedes teammate George Russell, saw his title chances take a critical blow when he retired from Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia with an engine failure, and a related grid penalty at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix will make his job tougher still.

Meanwhile, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc, Lando Norris and Max Verstappen all remain in mathematical contention for this year's championship, but face even tougher routes to the title than Russell due to their greater points deficits.

When could Antonelli win his first title?
In theory, the earliest Antonelli could seal the title is at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin later this month. In order to do so, he would need to grow his gap over Russell by 42 points in two race weekends, while outscoring Lewis Hamilton in third place by 20 points.

- Singapore Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch

- Valtteri Bottas cycles 400km from Malaysia to Singapore

- F1 cars to get software update after Malaysia 'bug'

Even with extra points on offer at the sprint race in Singapore this weekend, such a scenario would likely require victories for Antonelli and further retirements for Russell, while ensuring Hamilton is not in the fight for second place on the podium behind Antonelli. In addition, an Austin crowning would require Antonelli to make sure he is not outscored by three points by Leclerc, and six points by both Norris and Verstappen.

What does Antonelli need to claim the title?
Perhaps the easiest way to look at Antonelli's title run-in is that he needs to score 100 points over the remaining races to ensure he ends up as champion -- regardless of what any of his rivals manage.

With seven grands prix and a sprint race currently scheduled on the calendar, that route could be achieved with multiple different result combinations -- but for ease of an example, third place at every remaining race would comfortably see Antonelli over the line even if Russell wins at all seven grands prix and the sprint.

F1's rules state that if multiple drivers are tied on points, a countback of victories will decide who emerges on top. If the number of victories are also even, it then goes to second places, third places, fourth place, and so on. Currently, Antonelli has eight victories to Russell's three, although Russell has four second places to Antonelli's three. It's unlikely those countbacks will come into play, but it's why, currently, Antonelli needs 100 points rather than 99 to put the title entirely beyond Russell's grasp.

But how many races are actually left?
The situation is further complicated by question marks hanging over the final two races of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. F1 has made clear that it intends to finish the season as scheduled, but the ongoing war between the United States and Iran has the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

The same conflict led the cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in April, while Bahrain took the unusual approach of hosting its round 4,000 miles away from the island kingdom in Malaysia last weekend.

If Qatar and Abu Dhabi are also cancelled, F1's contingency plan is to host the final round of the season in Imola. Such a scenario would remove 25 of the potential points on offer, meaning Antonelli would only need 75 points between now and the end of the season to be crowned champion. Austin would still be the earliest round at which he could clinch the title, but it would come with a more achievable target of outscoring Russell by 17 points across the Singapore and U.S. race weekends rather than 42.

stories.headline: Tampa Bay Rays troll New York Yankees with signature Sinatra song after ALDS win
stories.summary: Someone in the Rays' clubhouse had a certain song ready to go after the team's 4-3 win over the Yankees at Yankee Stadium.
stories.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays are spreadin' the news.

On Wednesday night, the Rays completed a three-game sweep of the New York Yankees, winning a 4-3 nail-biter. Victor Mesa Jr.'s two-run home run in the top of the sixth inning put Tampa Bay ahead for good, while Anthony Volpe's potential game-tying homer in the bottom of that inning was overturned due to a fan interfering with the ball -- a different outcome than what happened with Jeffrey Maier during the 1996 American League Championship Series between the Yankees and Baltimore Orioles.

After the game, the Rays celebrated hard in the visitors clubhouse at Yankee Stadium -- and whoever was in charge of the music added a little salt to the home team's wounds.

That's Frank Sinatra's version of "(Theme From) New York, New York," which the Yankees play to celebrate a win at home. For one night, at least, it heralded something far different. The Rays will look to carry their momentum forward in the ALCS against either the Cleveland Guardians or Chicago White Sox.

stories.headline: Wysh List: What NHL execs think of ESPN's top 100 player rankings
stories.summary: Who was too high or too low according to actual team personnel and players? Plus, winners and losers of the week, key upcoming games and more.
stories.body:
"Why do you do this to yourselves?"

That was the first reaction from an NHL general manager as he perused the latest NHL Rank, the top 100 player list that publishes at the start of every season. It was a reaction that signaled some discontent with the ranking -- and he wasn't alone -- as well as a twinge of sympathy for the inevitable backlash that accompanies such an undertaking.

Here's the method to this madness: 15 individuals from the ESPN hockey family, from front-facing talents to ink-drenched scribes to analytics virtuosi, submitted their own ranking of the top 100 NHL players based on how well they're expected to perform in the 2026-27 regular season. Those ballots are combined to come up with a final Top 100.

So, in theory, this is a projection of greatness rather than a coronation for past efforts. Does that explain why Connor Hellebuyck, currently suspended by the Winnipeg Jets after a trade request, could be ranked 22nd if he's not even playing? Well, no, it doesn't, but then there are plenty of other questions for those who debated it this week.

I spoke with several NHL executives about this year's ranking. They had questions of their own.

"Why is Alex Ovechkin ranked here? Like, at all?" one executive asked.

The Washington Capitals' captain was ranked No. 78.

"He barely skates anymore. Ovechkin being on this list is silly. What year is this?"

Oh, c'mon ... let the man retire with dignity!

Another NHL executive believed there was another glaring gaffe in the ranking: New York Islanders phenom Matthew Schaefer at No. 16. Last season's rookie of the year had 59 points in 82 games while skating 24:41 per night. That ice time ranked 14th among all defensemen, and many of those defensemen who skated more finished well behind the 19-year-old in this ranking.

"Not many young defensemen have that kind of impact, that early," they said.

Speaking of Schaefer: "So two of the top six defensemen in the NHL got cut by Hockey Canada? Because Colton Parayko, Travis Sanheim and Drew Doughty are nowhere to be found on this list, and they all played in the Olympics," pondered one NHL executive, in reference to Schaefer and Evan Bouchard of the Edmonton Oilers.

(For what it's worth, Doughty made last year's list at No. 54 while the others did not.)

A few other reactions to our player ranking from NHL front office suits:

Two execs believed that the voters had succumbed to the siren's song of scoring, rather than accounting for the actual sway players have over their team's fortunes. "I think you have some high rankings on players who have more points scored than actual impact," one GM said. Another team exec lamented: "Too many empty-calorie point guys that don't drive winning," while specifically calling out Montreal winger Cole Caufield (25th).
A few players were cited by multiple NHL executives as being undervalued in this ranking: New York Rangers defenseman Adam Fox (51), Vegas Golden Knights winger Mark Stone (73) and Tampa Bay Lightning winger Brandon Hagel (55). "Brandon Hagel is a superstar, and people don't realize it. Way too low," one executive said.
More than one exec noted that our ranking of the 100 best players didn't exactly honor the reigning Stanley Cup champions, the Carolina Hurricanes. Center Sebastian Aho (48) was the only Cane to crack the top 50, and he was down from 28th on last year's list. Jaccob Slavin (62), Seth Jarvis (74), Andrei Svechnikov (84) and Nikolaj Ehlers (96) also made the cut. "Where's anyone from the best line from the reigning Cup winners?" one executive asked, referring to the trio of Taylor Hall, Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake.

I'm not going to deny there are a few shots that missed the net on this list. Schaefer is way too high. So is Martin Necas of the Colorado Avalanche at 24th; he had a career year skating 82% of the time with Nathan MacKinnon -- a luxury not afforded to several wingers ranked behind him. Would I have Brandt Clarke ranked ahead of Shea Theodore? I would not. Would I have had Darren Raddysh on this list at all, let alone at No. 90? I also would not.

On the flippity flop, Leo Carlson (36th) and Stone should be much higher. I would have liked Florida defenseman Seth Jones somewhere on this list -- although perhaps the toxic stink cloud from his time with the Blackhawks still follows him in South Florida despite helping the Panthers to their second Stanley Cup win.

But here's my scorching hot take on this year's NHL Rank on ESPN. Prepare yourself. Maybe get a tall glass of milk to handle the ghost pepper sear of this take.

The NHL Rank list is overall pretty ... good?

Qualms and quibbles aside, the top of the list seems about right. Proper respect was given to emerging talents (Macklin Celebrini at No. 4 and Nick Suzuki at No. 19) and established stars (Sidney Crosby, hanging tough at No. 23). Heck, we even found a way to get Evgeni Malkin in at No. 100, so Pittsburgh fans can finally extinguish the torches they light whenever this ranking dropped without him in it.

During my conversations around the league about the list, I found out I wasn't alone.

"This looks absolutely fine to me. I've got nothing to criticize here," one NHL assistant general manager said.

An NHL veteran player who scanned the list agreed.

"I think everyone is actually where they should be," the player said when shown the top 100. "It's a nice list. No notes."

Based on my texts, my inbox and my mentions, everyone else had more than enough notes to share. Some even without profanity!

Jump ahead:

Winners, losers of the week

Favorite on-ice moment

Must-see games

Puck headlines

WINNERS AND LOSERS
Winner: Alex Ovechkin
Last season, Ovechkin explicitly didn't want a farewell tour because he felt his pursuit of Wayne Gretzky's record in 2024-25 overshadowed everything about the Capitals, including his teammates. But after deciding in the summer that this season would be his last in the NHL, Ovi decided to just put the issue to bed early, sparing his teammates from questions about his status for the next 80-plus games.

It also sets up the NHL for a one-of-a-kind farewell tour. Consider other recent transcendent stars. Wayne Gretzky didn't let his fate be known until there were just a few games left in the 1998-99 season. Mario Lemieux played until he couldn't. Jaromir Jagr was an afterthought on the Calgary Flames before spending the next decade in Kladno, Czechia. Ovechkin will visit 31 other teams for the final time, giving fans the chance to react to his last NHL days.

That includes what could be the emotional apex of his season on April 4 in Washington's home finale against Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin and the Pittsburgh Penguins. If you don't have tickets and want to attend, prepare to sell a kidney.

Loser: Brady Tkachuk
The Florida Panthers didn't have a regulation loss in their first four games (2-0-2). Their losses were on the roster. Aleksander Barkov's lower-body injury thankfully wasn't as bad as feared, but their best player is still on the shelf for about six weeks. Brad Marchand was helped off the ice Tuesday after collisions with the net and the boards in Los Angeles. As of this writing, his status was unknown, but it didn't look good.

Another point of concern through four games: Brady Tkachuk has put out more podcasts (two) than put up points (zero), despite leading the Panthers with 11 shots. Granted, the loss of Barkov in Game 2 affected him -- witness Sam Reinhart also sporting goose eggs on his stat line through four games -- but Tkachuk was acquired to help the Panthers through significant lineup losses like they had last season. Plus, he has had to watch his old friends in Ottawa thriving in his absence.

Tkachuk will be fine. But it's not the start he or the Panthers wanted statistically.

Winner: GQ covers hockey
It's always interesting to see how a writer who doesn't cover hockey processes our silly little sport. Nick Remsen of GQ profiled San Jose Sharks star Macklin Celebrini, and gave NHL fans some artful new descriptions of backhand shots ("[He] pushed the puck into the net with the convex side of his blade, body twisting with near balletic torque...") and routine goal celebrations ("He was so happy after ricocheting a puck into the net's far outer edge that he all but flung himself into the sideboards...").

Loser: GQ makes it weird
Given the "Heated Rivalry" and "Off Campus" phenomenon and the NHL's now shuttered "Hot For Hockey" experiment, it's not out of bounds to ask someone like Macklin about the para-social relationship between fans and players. Where things got weird in the Celebrini profile: Asking about the "fan fiction element" in his fandom. Given the content in some of those stories, that question felt invasive and put him in an awkward spot.

Celebrini understandably punted on the answer, which isn't something for which he should have to answer anyway. Besides, it's not as if fan fiction involving NHL players started with Macklin Celebrini.

Winner: Dylan Larkin drama
A few sources around the league I spoke with previously didn't believe we'd see Larkin wear a Detroit sweater again, but the now-former Red Wings captain returned to the lineup from injury Tuesday night, his first game since requesting a trade from Detroit. The fans booed him as they booed him on opening night when he was introduced in street clothes; Larkin responded with a goal and an assist to reignite the dormant Detroit offense.

There were some cheers interspersed with the boos when he was announced as the No. 1 star. After the game, Larkin said, "I'm just happy to be a hockey player today and go out and try to help the team win."

Give Larkin this credit: He has spoken to reporters. He has faced the fans. He wore a uniform that he has asked to no longer wear. How this all ends up is anyone's guess, but we're here for the soap opera: "As The Winged Wheel Turns."

Loser: No-trade clauses
The aftermath of Larkin's trade request was put into sharp relief last week when NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said the league is monitoring how players are using their no-movement and no-trade clauses. Larkin, then Detroit's captain, asked out with five years left on an eight-year contract, and limited the field of suitors to three teams with his no-trade clause.

Just like how the NHL enacted offside reviews because one player (Matt Duchene) was a country mile offside and the officials missed it, Larkin's trade request appears to have lit the fuse for this potentially contentious labor dispute.

What I can report: Bettman is speaking to players to get feedback on the way trade protection is currently being used and potential changes to the system down the line. It'll be fascinating to hear how they feel about Larkin's gambit.

Favorite on-ice moment

It's always fascinating to see what the league's preeminent agitators use for material. Ottawa forward Nick Cousins pantomiming the letter "C" and pointing to his chest as he taunts Dylan Larkin getting the captaincy stripped from him? Chef's kiss, especially if you want to add the subtext of having reminded Larkin that he's stuck in some kind of trade demand purgatory.

Must-see games coming up

Toronto Maple Leafs at Vegas Golden Knights

Thursday, 10 p.m. ET | ESPN+

The vibes are good for the Leafs. They're 2-2-0. Auston Matthews scored an overtime winner against Nashville in a game that saw No. 1 pick Gavin McKenna finally hit the scoresheet. But starting with this game against old pal Mitch Marner and the Golden Knights, we're going to learn about more about Toronto: The Leafs are at Colorado, at Utah and then get Buffalo at home.

Edmonton Oilers at San Jose Sharks

Saturday, 4 p.m. ET | ESPN+

Celebrini is day-to-day, and one hopes he's available for a showdown against Connor McDavid. But no matter his status: This is a four-point divisional game for the Sharks, and if they're going to be a playoff team then these are the games they need to win.

Colorado Avalanche at Dallas Stars

Tuesday, 8:30 p.m. ET | ESPN

The first meeting between the two best regular-season teams in the Central Division last season. Three of their four games in 2025-26 went to a shootout. An early test for both teams.

From your hockey friends at ESPN

Ryan Clark went to Houston to find out why that city believes it deserves an NHL expansion team more than Austin, Texas, does. Said Mayor John Whitmire on what the city will do to get a team: "We're not going to start selling dope out of an arena or anything. But if it's lawful, we'll pull that trigger."
Sean Allen looks at hits and blocks in fantasy hockey, and who could be the most valuable players this season to that end.
Kalan Hooks with a wild story out of New Jersey, as a youth hockey team owner is under fire after threatening to suspend the children on his under-10 hockey team after their parents created their own merchandise.
Finally, Rachel Kryshak has a deep dive into which NCAA teams have the most high-end talent. How did we end up with so many kids named "Ryker" playing hockey?

Jersey Foul

I appreciate the integration of Larkin's name into this Protest Jersey about his trade request. Much more impressive than just using the "L" and taping the word "LOSER" on the back or just covering the whole thing with the word "TRAITOR," which is what other fans decided to do.

Puck headlines
DATELINE: TEAM USA GROUP CHAT
One of the greatest bits of hockey lore going these days is the power of the U.S. men's Olympic team group chat, which has been credited with having players like Winnipeg Jets goalie Connor Hellebuyck demand a trade to the U.S.

Gold medalist Vincent Trocheck of the Utah Mammoth says he believes its power is overstated.

"I think people make it a bigger thing than it is," he told me this week. "Obviously, people want the headlines, but the whole Canada thing or guys wanting out of Canada that are from the U.S., I think it was more situational than it was anything else."

But is there a thriving group chat among the players?

"There's one from Team USA. But not, like, a trade talk one," he said. "It's been dormant for a little bit. It's sad. I might have to fire it back up."

DATELINE: CONNOR HELLEBUYCK
It was a bit surprising when Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff didn't rule out the possibility that Hellebuyck could remain with the team after going public with a trade demand.

But one former teammate of the star goaltender I spoke with actually didn't rule it out.

The thinking here: Hellebuyck will eventually grow frustrated with losing pay after having been suspended by the Jets, as it has been reported he'll lose around $39,000 a day. But more than that, he's still on friendly terms with his teammates -- some of them neighbors -- who theoretically would welcome back the multitime Vezina Trophy winner if he decides to pull a Larkin and suit up again.

DATELINE: UTAH MAMMOTH
One sign the Mammoth are really starting to thrive in Salt Lake City? The lack of enemy fans in the stands. Team president Chris Armstrong told me that when Utah opened its season against the Blackhawks at home, there were very few Chicago fans in the building "in comparison to the inaugural season" in Salt Lake City.

"I feel like maybe that people are switching their allegiance to the Mammoth now," Armstrong said.

If they keep playing the way they're playing to start the season, who wouldn't?

The Wysh List is created by senior writer Greg Wyshynski and appears every Thursday on ESPN.com and the ESPN app.

stories.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'I still have the scar' from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.

The Spaniard, whose new four-year contract at the Emirates was announced on Wednesday, took the club to their first Champions League final for 20 years last season but saw his team defeated on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Echoing the words of the last man to take them to the brink of elite European glory -- Arsène Wenger, who previously said that "every defeat is a scar in your heart" -- Arteta told The Athletic: "I still have the scar, like Arsène says.

"I still have that poison in my veins. It has to stay there because that's when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody."

Looking towards the future, Arteta added that he was excited for a number of different aspects of the club's growth.

"Globally, with our supporters? Great. How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we're going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great," he said.

"But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite."

He added: "It feels like it's still a lot to do, and it's just the beginning."

Arteta has, however, already managed to do something no Arsenal manager had achieved for 22 years: win a league title.

"It wasn't just a trophy. It was a moment that we're going to remember for the rest of our lives," he said.

Asked what game from his Arsenal tenure he would relive, the 44-year-old chose the controversial 1-0 win over West Ham which put the Gunners on the brink of returning to the top of the perch.

"This is football elevated to its best version, when a journey, a moment that can change so many people's lives, goes one way or the other," he said. "You just pray because you know if it goes the wrong side, probably it's gone again.

"That day when I went home, I said, 'We're going to be champions. It is our year. This has happened for a reason, and we're going to get it done.'"
