stories.headline: Saints trade ruckman to Cats, chase on for star Swan
stories.summary: Geelong have brokered a trade for St Kilda ruckman Rowan Marshall, further depleting the Cats' draft stocks as Swans defender Nick Blakey eyes a move.
stories.body:
St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No. 14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

Cats football boss Andrew Mackie on Monday indicated an unwillingness to part with their first-round pick for Marshall after the Saints asked for a player to be attached to the trade.

St Kilda football boss Lenny Hayes hailed the fair return for Marshall, who has played 177 AFL games since being a rookie pick at age 21.

"We are pleased to have achieved (adequate compensation) by bringing in another first round selection, alongside our existing pick at eight," Hayes said.

Geelong needed to bolster their ruck stocks, with Rhys Stanley retiring and 21-year-old Mitchell Edwards still finding his feet at the level.

The Cats are among five clubs eyeing Nick Blakey as the Swans defender tests the water for a possible trade.

The 2024 All-Australian was one of five players who served a club-imposed ban through the AFL finals for breaching the club's behavioural standards at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne.

The 26-year-old has since been linked to a move despite being signed to Sydney until 2031.

Swans list boss Chris Keane said the club had not been told Blakey was meeting with rival clubs this week, but remained in talks with his manager Robbie D'Orazio.

"As we sit here right now, these are all hypotheticals," he told Trade Radio.

"It's certainly not something we've actively pursued, and we feel confident that he could walk back into our footy club.

"But given the calibre of player that he is, and the fact that he is contracted for five more years, we feel like making any deal happen would be significantly challenging."

Blakey's preferred option is reportedly Geelong, but the Cats have limited draft capital after executing trades for Marshall and Essendon's Jordan Ridley.

North Melbourne have expressed interest for Blakey, whose father John played in the Kangaroos' 1996 and 1999 premierships across 224 club games.

Essendon are another suitor, with Blakey's former mentors Mark McVeigh and John Longmire joining the club and the Bombers boasting salary cap room following the exits of Zach Merrett and Ridley.

"We haven't had any indication off Nick's management that he's looking to leave Sydney," Essendon list boss Matt Rosa told Trade Radio.

"But certainly we've had some discussions internally and we'll continue to do that."

Blakey has reportedly already met with Gold Coast coach Damien Hardwick, while St Kilda are also expected to make contact.

Any trade for Blakey would likely need to be approved by a club board, given the ongoing police investigation into an alleged sexual assault at the hotel.

Swans vice-captain Isaac Heeney, star midfielder Chad Warner, tagger James Jordon and Blakey were interviewed by police but no charges have been laid.

Riley Bice, another Swan banned for round 24 and the finals campaign, is not being investigated.

In other developments, young Hawk Aidan Schubert has agreed to be traded to Gold Coast in a separate deal that is expected to allow Ben King join Hawthorn as a free agent.

The Suns' 72-hour window to match the Hawks' offer for King or accept compensation, likely pick No. 7 in the draft, ends at 4.15pm (AEDT) on Friday.

The Western Bulldogs are yet to file free agency paperwork for Port Adelaide's Zak Butters ahead of Friday afternoon's deadline.

Port can accept draft compensation, which would currently deliver pick No.5, or match the Bulldogs' offer and force a trade.

The trade period closes on Wednesday evening.

stories.headline: Silva rises in P4P women's top 10, making most of golden opportunity
stories.summary: After winning UFC women's flyweight title, Silva rises in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
The women's flyweight division might be the most stacked weight class in the UFC, and Natalia Silva wears the gold.

Silva was too fast, too precise and too elusive for Wang Cong in the UFC 332 main event on Saturday, and as a result, the 29-year-old from Brazil captured the vacant 125-pound title. She moves up one position to No. 4 in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

Silva is one of seven flyweights in the women's top 10. The division with the next most pound-for-pound elites is lightweight, with three fighters in the men's rankings.

The top two fighters on the women's list are Valentina Shevchenko, who vacated the UFC title last month while healing shoulder and back injuries, and Zhang Weili, a two-time former strawweight titlist who last fought at flyweight, in an unsuccessful challenge of Shevchenko in November.

Aside from Silva, there are three other UFC flyweights in the top 10 (Alexa Grasso, Manon Fiorot and Erin Blanchfield), and the rankings also include PFL 125-pounder Dakota Ditcheva.

UFC women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison has been missing from these rankings for the past few months because, with no fights since June 2025, she is ineligible. But Harrison will return from neck surgery to defend her title against former two-division champion and consensus GOAT Amanda Nunes at UFC 334 on Nov. 14.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Oct. 7. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which Natalia Silva captured by beating Wang Cong at UFC 332. When Shevchenko is healed up, she'll be looking to take back the belt.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Previous ranking: 4

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her upcoming bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Natalia Silva; 5. Cris Cyborg; 6. Alexa Grasso; 7. Manon Fiorot; 8. Dakota Ditcheva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Silva; 4. Zhang; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Andrew Davis: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Fiorot; 9. Blanchfield; 10. Suarez.

Dre Waters: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Fiorot; 10. Suarez.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Ditcheva.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (38) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch at UFC 331. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight on the White House lawn. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from a challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Joshua Van; 7. Arman Tsarukyan; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Pereira; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Van; 8. Gane; 9. Yan; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Tom Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Topuria; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Tsarukyan.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Van; 5. Gaethje; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Tsarukyan; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Volkanovski.

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: WNBA playoffs 2026: After another early exit, what's next for Fever?
stories.summary: Despite a dominant offense and Caitlin Clark's return, the Fever suffered another early playoff exit. What's next for Indiana?
stories.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- A week ago, ahead of a deciding Game 3 against the Las Vegas Aces, Indiana Fever forward Myisha Hines-Allen laid out the franchise's expectations plainly.

"There's always going to be room for growth, but with how [GM] Amber [Cox] put this team together, it's championship or bust," Hines-Allen said before the game. "We're all trying to win this championship this year."

After a semifinal appearance in 2025, a season in which star Caitlin Clark sat out most of the year injured, hopes were high for 2026.

And sure enough, the Fever had the No. 1 offense in WNBA history, averaging 96.0 points per game in the regular season. Kelsey Mitchell (24.7 points per game) and Clark (22.3) finished ranked No. 2 and No. 3 in points per game and were the highest-scoring teammates in league history.

But throughout, off-court drama surrounded the team. Then a swoon in the final days of the regular season dropped the Fever to the No. 6 seed, facing the defending champion Aces in a best-of-three first round.

After the Game 3 loss, a back-and-forth affair, the Fever were left reckoning with a season that ended earlier than any of them hoped.

Within 48 hours of the season-ending loss, another controversy had developed: After Cox issued a strong defense of the Fever fanbase in her end-of-season availability, Mitchell seemed to contradict it, referencing troubling fan behavior and the intense microscope that comes with playing alongside Clark. It was a fitting conclusion to a season of big dreams and bitter disappointments in which the focus could never just be on basketball.

"Not every season's perfect," Aliyah Boston said Saturday after the season's end. "You're going to have your ups and downs, but we really stuck together through it all. Like no matter what. Obviously, when you look back at games that you wish that you didn't drop early, and maybe that would have been a difference. ... But here we are, right? There's nothing we can do right now."

ON THE COURT, at least one half of the Fever's plan went perfectly.
The offense was formidable, and Clark's return went better than anyone could have hoped. Mitchell set the league record for the most points scored (1,086) and the most 3-point field goals (135) while scoring 20-plus points in a WNBA-record 27 consecutive games. Boston was an All-Star for the fourth consecutive year with a career-high 16.1 points per game, grabbed 8.0 rebounds and extended her range beyond the 3-point line and shot 40.6%.

Clark was the first player in the history of the league to score 40-plus points with 10-plus assists in a single game; her five games of 30-plus points and 10-plus assists this season are more than any other player in league history combined. She became the league's first player to record 800-plus points and 300-plus assists in a single season.

Clark called 2026 one of the most fulfilling years of her career. She played more basketball than ever as she rehabbed. She played in Team USA camps, 40 regular-season games and was selected for the FIBA World Cup team that won gold in September. A worrisome back issue flared up early in the season but proved not to be a long-term issue. The defensive part of her game was highly criticized early in the season as teams specifically targeted her, but even that improved incrementally. A sneaky midrange game began to appear as the season went on to complement the drives to the basket and the step-back 3s.

Clark's first signature shoe with Nike, the Caitlin 1, released last week.

"I didn't play much last year, but I was able to come out here and put together the best season I've had," Clark said, "and perform at a really high level and basically get better in every area and still feel like I have so many areas to improve.

"I guess that's the most exciting part moving forward."

The old saying, though, goes that defense wins championships, and that was the problem all season for the Fever. They ranked No. 11 in points allowed per game (90.4) and No. 8 in defensive rating (108.3). The Aces scored 102 and 94 in Game 1 and 3 victories to eliminate Indiana.

And off the court, the Fever were constantly barraged with distractions or drama. For much of the season, it felt like those 40 minutes between the lines -- win or lose -- were the most peaceful, normal times of the summer for this group.

"Obviously, we weathered a lot," Clark said. "There's always so much outside noise and a microscope of how we perform every single day, and a lot of really good moments, a lot of tough moments, too."

SINCE CLARK WAS drafted No. 1 in 2024, the Fever have had an inordinate amount of attention on the organization from both WNBA fans and entities that rarely paid attention to the league in the past. Clark's name was recently, and randomly, brought up in the middle of a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing.

It's been a boon for the Fever, who have become the most popular team in the league thanks in large part to her fame -- quickly acknowledged by all those around the team, including Cox.

"The other piece about Caitlin that I never want to take for granted is just what she has meant to our team, what she has meant to the league, and what she's meant to women's basketball," she said. "She remains the tipping point. You look at the ratings and you look at the full buildings, that started in 2024 when she came into the league, and that is because of Caitlin Clark."

But it can also lead to increased scrutiny on Clark and the rest of the team, as happened multiple times this season.

In June, the relationship between Stephanie White and Clark was questioned after the coach was seen in an animated discussion with the point guard during a 16-point loss to the Portland Fire. Both downplayed it as two competitive people in the heat of the moment. Clark and assistant coach Briann January also had fiery interactions on the sideline that begat questions regarding the franchise player and the coaching staff.

The focus on the Fever's play -- and White -- continued throughout the season. Then, in June, Sophie Cunningham kicked off another round of headlines for the Fever. Cunningham, a popular personality on social media and her podcast, has no problem being an agitator. T-shirts featuring her pointing at DeWanna Bonner after a heated game against the Phoenix Mercury in June became a hot commodity at Fever games at home and on the road.

But one moment affected not only the Fever, but the entire league. In an ESPN article published in July, Cunningham discussed, among other things, how to "protect women's sports" and said: "I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I'm like, 'I never once said that.' I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

It became a seasonlong topic with coaches and players being asked their opinions around the league. Protests both for and against began forming outside arenas when the Fever would play on the road. Seattle Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton was suspended from attending five home games after her exchange with a pair of fans who brought signs into Climate Pledge Arena supporting Cunningham with the Fever in town for a road game in late July.

All these issues and more -- 11 Republican lawmakers sent WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert a letter in July demanding the league take "accountability" for "multiple attacks" against Clark -- came to a head just after the All-Star break.

In a game on Aug. 8, Cunningham took a hit around the head and neck on a fast-break layup from DiJonai Carrington. The particularly hard contact started a dustup on the court; Carrington was issued a flagrant 2 and ejected from the game. Moments later, Carrington posted on her Threads account: "WHITE PRIVILEGE @indianafever." Postgame, White acknowledged it was a hard foul, but said she didn't think Carrington intentionally went for the neck.

Fever fans accused White of not supporting her players. Indiana Lt. Gov. Micah Beckwith tweeted, "Ok... The @IndianaFever need to let Stephanie White go. No solid coach would ever take the side of the opposing team's player who committed a flagrant foul on one of your own players. Terrible coaching! The Fever need to defend their players."

During the next home game, on Aug. 11 against the New York Liberty, boos rained down on Gainbridge Arena. The disdain was focused on White during pregame introductions. Before that game, White had used her pregame media session to respond to the noise; team president Kelly Krauskopf issued a statement with full support for White that same day.

"The hate, the fearmongering, the divisiveness, the stuff that's trying to hijack our league will not win," White said before the game, pounding her fist on a table multiple times.

"We are united. We are connected. We will not be divided," she added. "Every day, these women put their ass on the line. Every day, when they go low, we go high. Love will win, grace will win, humility will win, and kindness will win. I stand by them. I will always stand by them.

"Everybody else can go to hell."

EVERY SEASON WITH Clark on the team will have championship expectations, a side effect of having a generational player on the roster. But every season with Clark, through no fault of her own, also brings a level of outside noise that organizations will have to navigate.

That was evident on Saturday, during Mitchell's end-of-season availability.

Compared with her interviews after the Game 3 loss, the weight seemed lifted from Mitchell's shoulders as she smiled and acknowledged that she would be "selfish" in her approach to unrestricted free agency.

Mitchell -- the Fever's No. 2 player in points and assists, No. 1 in 3-point field goals and No. 4 in steals in franchise history -- said the climate in Indiana can be challenging.

"Showing up every day to compete for fans that may or may not like you is hard," Mitchell said.

Earlier Saturday, in her own availability, Cox had effusively praised Clark and ended her session with a staunch defense of Fever fans that have received criticism for their behavior toward opposing players.

"The attacks on our fanbase have no basis in reality, and they need to stop," she said.

Former Fever player Brianna Turner, now a member of the Aces, disputed Cox's sentiments on social media. "This is an unequivocally false statement," wrote Turner, who serves as treasurer of the Women's National Basketball Players Association. "Players inside and outside the organization have repeatedly issued complaints with the Fever fanbase. While it's not all Indy fans, it's certainly a trend. To say the attacks have 'no basis in reality' is disingenuous."

Along with Mitchell, Cunningham, Tyasha Harris and Hines-Allen are all unrestricted free agents this winter -- meaning, like everything in the orbit of the Fever, the offseason could be dramatic.

Cox has said her priority is bringing back Mitchell and keeping the Fever's big three together.

Clark's play has made her eligible for the "EPIC" (Exceptional Performance on Initial Contract) provision of the new collective bargaining agreement that allows players to renegotiate the fourth year of their rookie deal and sign a three-year extension. Players who have been named All-WNBA first team or second team are eligible for a max deal or the supermax if named MVP.

"Caitlin has earned the opportunity to sign her EPIC extension, so we're really excited to talk to her and her team about that," Cox said. "She had an MVP-caliber season, and it was wonderful to see coming off of her injury."

As for Cunningham, Cox said the off-court conversations surrounding her will not impact the evaluation of the player. Through the first two months of the season, Cunningham was considered a Sixth Player of the Year candidate before she cooled over the last two months. Both Cox and White pointed to help on the wing as an offseason priority.

"Sophie's had two really productive years for us in terms of shooting the basketball," Cox said. "She is a really solid leader in the locker room, a great connector. She brings levity, but also brings a lot of experience. She's serious and is an important voice in our locker room when we need it. When we really need to lock in.

"She's an unrestricted free agent, so we look forward to having those conversations. Again, she had a really productive year, and we'll see just where things take us."

White, too, will be part of the conversations about the Fever's future. She just finished her second year at the helm, and 2025 was considered an overachievement, advancing to within one game of the Finals with an infirmary ward of a roster. The past five months have been considered a disappointment with a first-round exit and questions swirling around her job stability.

"There were some highlights, and there are things we never need to get better at," Cox said after the season. "We're all going to get in the room and get back to the drawing board and we're going to address some of those and make sure that we're ready to go when next season starts. And that includes Steph and the coaching staff."

"I feel support from the organization, no doubt about that," White said after the season. "At the end of the day, it's their decision about whether I return or not. I'd love the opportunity. I love this franchise. I have always felt supported from this franchise, and I hope to continue to be the coach."

This all awaits Cox in what will undoubtedly be another busy offseason. A new practice facility is scheduled to open before 2027 training camp. Cox wants to add frontcourt depth to help Boston and Makayla Timpson, and a three-and-D wing is also on the wish list. Despite expectations, the Fever were light on playoff experience and there's optimism that it was gained the hard way. The hope is to continue to develop the young talent, build through the draft and supplement through free agency.

After a season with unfulfilled goals and more drama than anyone was thrilled about, there's an understandable wonder of how much could change.

"When you talk about the noise around this team, I think that's just a product of becoming mainstream," Cox said. "People care. I've been a part of this league for many, many years, and you could have a trade, you could have a bad loss and nobody cared. Nobody was writing about it. Nobody was tweeting about it, and that was bad. Apathy was bad.

"So, what comes with the quote-unquote noise? I would call it just a lot of people caring."

stories.headline: Rockets, Mavs take China: Highlights, top scenes from off the court
stories.summary: The top sights and sounds from the Dallas Mavericks and Houston Rockets' preseason trip to China.
stories.body:
The NBA preseason slate sends the Dallas Mavericks and Houston Rockets across the world for a doubleheader in Macao, China, on Oct. 9 and 11.

Houston and Dallas are the second set of teams to play in Macao. The Phoenix Suns and Brooklyn Nets competed in the gambling hub last season, marking the return of the NBA to China after a yearslong hiatus. Similar to last year, the Rockets and Mavericks will be playing at Macao's Venetian Arena.

A trip overseas tends to bring a team closer together ahead of the long grind of the regular season. While the preseason action might not indicate how a team performs when the games begin to count, it's the off-court activities that can make an impact in the end.

Here's a look at the top sights and sounds from the Rockets-Mavericks trip in Macao.

A hometown welcome

With a flight time that can reach or exceed 20 hours, finally touching ground can be a relief. When each respective team arrived at their hotels, fans made sure to show the players love.

Room tour from an unlikely source

Rockets' fans got an inside look at the rooms for each player courtesy of big man Steven Adams. The 6-foot-11 center shared a video of his setup, which included a bowl of fruit, Rockets-themed pillow and Egyptian cotton.

Picture-perfect setting and love for Kyrie and Durant

It's not a trip to a new location without a memorable group photo. The Mavericks and Rockets separately posed near a body of water with the Venetian Macao set in the background.

As Dallas snapped its picture, fans flocked to greet the team -- specifically, star guard Kyrie Irving. The same occurred for Houston star Kevin Durant.

Mavs making presence felt

After the first practice in Macao for the Mavericks, the team already needed to find replacements for two items: a chair and a rim. Forward Naji Marshall broke a rim, explaining "I'm too strong and I've got too much power," before he signed it and the team collected it. Marshall then broke a chair while sitting down.

Adams and Bogdanović take in Macao

The Rockets center and his teammate Bogdan Bogdanović made sure to look around Macao to get a feel for the city. They went to the ruins of Saint Paul's, which is the facade of what was originally the church of Mater Dei built between 1602 to 1640. The duo then had some street food, all while a huge crowd followed along.

Views from Hong Kong

It takes 55 minutes to an hour to travel from Macao to Hong Kong via a ferry. A Dallas quartet of Daniel Gafford, Caleb Martin, Dwight Powell and Sergio de Larrea took advantage of the distance. The group traveled to Victoria Peak in Hong Kong.

Yao Ming ... is still growing?

The Rockets legend visited the NBA Macao house with fellow Rockets great Cuttino Mobley. While at the venue, Mobley found a cardboard cutout of the 7-foot-6 center. Remarkably, when Yao approached it, it seemed like he had grown. He joked: "I have something in my shoes."

KD, Kyrie hang out

The two future Hall of Famers shared a moment together on the court in Macao, chatting it up and laughing.

For the kids
Young fans were more than thrilled to meet their heroes in Macao, and both Durant and Flagg were happy to oblige.

stories.headline: Jayden Daniels will be 'full go' vs. Giants, says Commanders OC
stories.summary: Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough said Jayden Daniels will have no limitations when the star QB plays Sunday against the Giants.
stories.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Washington Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough said Jayden Daniels will have no limitations when the star quarterback plays Sunday against the New York Giants.

"He's full go," Blough said Thursday when asked if Washington had to account for Daniels' dislocated left elbow in the game plan. "We're looking forward to having him back."

Daniels was a full participant in practice Wednesday and was expected to be one all week with the idea that he'll start Sunday against the Giants (3-1). The Commanders (1-3) have endured another injury-filled season, with Daniels already having missed two games because of his non-throwing elbow injury.

Daniels suffered the injury in Washington's Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys; he had initially dislocated it in Week 9 last season.

Because he has suffered the same injury twice, Daniels will wear a black brace that leaves his elbow slightly bent. Last week, Daniels said the brace won't limit him when handing off or taking snaps from center.

The quarterbacks start each practice by taking snaps from under center, and Daniels was doing that last week as well as Wednesday. Daniels said he is getting used to the brace, which is different from the one he wore last season when he returned in Week 14 vs. Minnesota.

Daniels will need to wear the brace the rest of the season. He has talked since training camp opened about being smarter when running in games. His game has been built on dynamic play -- running when needed, whether designed or scrambling.

stories.headline: George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to run different Mercedes packages at Singapore Grand Prix
stories.summary: Title rivals Kimi Antonelli and George Russell will drive different specifications of Mercedes' Formula 1 car at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix as the team searches for answers over its lack of performance in Malaysia.
stories.body:
Title rivals Kimi Antonelli and George Russell will drive different specifications of Mercedes' Formula 1 car at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix as the team searches for answers over its lack of performance in Malaysia.

Antonelli will run the upgraded aerodynamic package that the team debuted last weekend, while Russell will revert to the previous specification that won races in Monza, Madrid and Baku.

The team hopes that running a comparison between the two cars will help it understand why the new package did not perform as expected in Malaysia and allow it to define a longer-term development direction.

Russell is Antonelli's closest rival in this year's drivers' championship, although a power unit failure in Malaysia saw him fall 84 points behind his teammate in the standings.

Russell claims he pushed for the two cars to run different specifications this weekend as soon as it became clear in Malaysia that the new package was not performing.

He said the decision then became a "no-brainer" when his power unit failure on Sunday meant he would be starting from the back of the grid in Singapore due to an engine penalty.

"Actually, I instigated the conversation prior to the race [in Malaysia] on Sunday," Russell said. "So when the failure happened it was kind of a no-brainer because we were 50-50 about it pre-race and I was more in favour to do it, and now it is a total no-brainer."

Russell suspects the lack of performance compared to rivals Red Bull in Malaysia was more track specific than a direct result of the upgrade, but welcomed the opportunity to return to the car specification he won with at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix two weeks ago.

"We're pretty confident it [the lack of performance] is Malaysia specific," he said. "When you look at the pace of Red Bull as well, they clearly overperformed compared to where they've been this season compared to all of the other teams.

"And actually when you look at our pace compared to McLaren and Ferrari it wasn't too dissimilar, it wasn't massively out of bed.

"So with this engine penalty this weekend has just given them a good opportunity to roll back, it's the car that I won in Baku with, so yeah that's it."

The upgrade package is the result of months of development work after Mercedes opted not to keep pace with the updates of its rivals and instead work towards a single significant step for the final third of the season.

The upgrades to the car are far-reaching, including a new floor, rear suspension, and noticeable changes to the upper bodywork of the car, including its engine cover.

- F1 cars to get software update after Malaysia 'bug' to prevent repeat at future races

- Singapore Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

- Rwanda F1 race: Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen welcome prospect of Africa return as talks gather pace

Antonelli believes the upgrade ultimately has more potential but still requires setup work to unlock it.

"It's just a matter of trying to put the car in the right window and understand it more," he said. "And this weekend, I think, is a good example. It's going to be a good opportunity to see and to compare the two packages, because we know the old one -- we've known it for ages.

"We know how to set up the car around that package, we know it works really well and it's really fast in these kind of tracks.

"And, you know, we really want to understand, on the other hand, this new package and trying to really extract the maximum out of it, because the team has done a tremendous job. They're doing so much work on this new package and it would be just a shame to write it off so early.

"So I feel like I'm quite comfortable on keeping it. And actually, you know, I really want to help the team out to understand it more and to, as I said before, try to extract the potential."

Russell, who has won three races to Antonelli's eight, said via PA, ahead of this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix: "The guy who's performed the best is the guy who's leading the championship.

"If you add up the numbers and the points, I still think I'd be very much in the game in an ordinary season. I still think I'd be on the back foot, but in the game for it to flip very quick.

"When you add up the points from this season that have been lost, you know, I've probably had more failures this year than I've had in the three seasons put together.

"Of course, it's tough to take. If I'm being 100% fair with myself, as I've said before, the performance this season hasn't been strong enough. And it probably would have affected me more if these results have ... Like, who knows if I'd have still been in the fight or not, in a more normal circumstance.

"But obviously the pressure and the momentum, every setback has an impact on that momentum.

"It's been pretty incredible how things have panned out this year. But you've just got to focus on what you can control."

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Previews and betting info for all 10 of Thursday's games
stories.summary: From the six 7 p.m. matchups all the way through Maple Leafs-Golden Knights at 10, here's what to watch.
stories.body:
It's Thursday, which means the NHL has a massive slate of games for fans to consume. This week there are 10 contests around the league, including six beginning at 7 p.m. ET.

From those six through to Toronto Maple Leafs-Vegas Golden Knights (with a 10 p.m. opening puck drop), here's a look at the key stats and storylines in each contest, along with betting info on broadcast details:

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Philadelphia Flyers at Ottawa Senators

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | OTT -142, O/U: 5.5

Both of these teams made the playoffs last season -- and one of them looks like it will be right back in the mix again. Led by Tim Stutzle, the Senators look like the real deal and almost appear as though the clean break from Brady Tkachuk this summer was a wise move from management. The Flyers, on the other hand, have yet to earn a win this season, and their -12 goal differential is second worst in the league -- ahead of only the Flames, who are assuredly in rebuilding mode. Does the tide turn on Thursday? Full preview

Utah Mammoth at Boston Bruins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | UTA -118, O/U: 5.5

The Mammoth burst onto the scene last year by earning the first playoff berth in franchise history and taking the eventual conference champion Golden Knights to six games in the first round. After some impressive performances in the first week of 2026-27, they've done nothing but gather support for their claim as a true contender. The next stop is in Boston, where the Bruins have had an uneven start: wins over the Rangers and Jets were followed by bad losses to the Wild and Senators. Which version of the B's shows up? Full preview

Dallas Stars at Buffalo Sabres

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | BUF -115, O/U: 5.5

The appearance of the Stars on the schedule brings about bad memories about 1999 for many Sabres fans, although several key members of the current roster weren't born when Brett Hull's controversial goal won the title for Dallas. As currently constructed, both of these teams should find their way back to the postseason this spring -- and perhaps another matchup in the Stanley Cup Final. Full preview

Nashville Predators at Montreal Canadiens

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MTL -185, O/U: 6.5

Each team brings a 1-1-1 record to this showdown, although fans of one of the teams are probably a lot less happy about that mark than the other's. In addition to the identical records, both teams have been driven by their stars so far. Steven Stamkos is the Preds' leading scorer, with three goals and one assist, while Nick Suzuki leads the way for the Habs with two goals and four assists. Full preview

Minnesota Wild at Tampa Bay Lightning

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | TB -148, O/U: 5.5

In the possible future world where these two clubs meet in the 2027 Stanley Cup Final, fans will have to look back to the early season for evidence of how they performed against one another. After this tilt, the pair will square off in Minnesota on Nov. 7, and then that's that. How likely is that Cup Final matchup? Stathletes projects it as having a 1.79% chance, which is 12th highest (Avalanche-Lightning currently leads the projections, at 7.17%). Full preview

Vancouver Canucks at Carolina Hurricanes

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CAR -325, O/U: 6.5

From one of the more likely Cup Final matchups to one of the least likely; the defending champs welcome the team that finished dead last in 2025-26. However, the Canucks haven't been the easy out that they were last season, with two wins in four games (and a one-goal loss to the Golden Knights). Carolina's Sebastian Aho was kept off the scoresheet in Game 1, but has four goals and three assists combined in the team's next three games. Does he stay hot in this one? Full preview

Chicago Blackhawks at New York Islanders

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NYI -185, O/U: 5.5

Had Connor Bedard not injured himself this offseason, this would have been a fun showdown between two of the game's most exciting young players. Instead, it'll just be Isles D-man Matthew Schaefer in the spotlight, as he continues to build on his impressive rookie campaign. And, as consolation, the Blackhawks do have a current rookie leading them in scoring, 2025's No. 3 pick Anton Frondell, with a goal and three assists through four games. Full preview

San Jose Sharks at St. Louis Blues

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+/Disney+/Hulu) | STL -130, O/U: 5.5

Last season, both the Sharks and Blues missed the final Western wild-card spot by four points. Ahead of opening puck drop, the Sharks are the current possessors of that wild card in the Western standings, with the Blues two points back. The good news for St. Louis fans: The team has 81 games remaining to make up that gap. Thus far, the Blues have been led in scoring by two offseason additions -- Connor McMichael and Mason McTavish -- while San Jose has been paced by Macklin Celebrini, who missed the recent loss to the Stars and is listed as "day-to-day" on the injury report. Full preview

Colorado Avalanche at Calgary Flames

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | COL -218, O/U: 6.5

Another game with lopsided expectations (as evidenced by that DraftKings line). Perhaps the simplest way to demonstrate: The Avs are averaging seven goals per game; at their current pace, the Flames won't score seven goals total until Game No. 7 this season. The Avs are allowing 2.5 goals per game; the Flames allow that many every 28 minutes. In other words, fantasy managers will want to be sure all of their Avs are in the active lineup -- even beyond the no-brainers like Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar and Martin Necas. Full preview

Toronto Maple Leafs at Vegas Golden Knights

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | VGK -162, O/U: 6.5

Maple Leafs-Golden Knights games last season took on added emphasis due to Mitch Marner's departure from Toronto to Vegas in summer 2025. That's less of a storyline this season; instead, this game will be another good litmus test for the Leafs as they push for a playoff return after last season's disappointment. This is not one of the more likely Cup Final matchups -- Stathletes projects it as a 0.02% chance -- but that number would assuredly rise if the Leafs keeping winning. Vegas' Jack Eichel leads all NHL scorers heading into Thursday, with 10 points through four games. Full preview

New hockey fans -- and maybe some veteran ones too -- might wonder why Florida Panthers fans throw plastic rats on the ice after home games.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Thursday, Oct. 8
Marshall lands at the Cats

St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No.14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

-- AAP

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Matchmaking, inactivity -- and, yes, fights -- shift MMA divisional rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
The fighter who won a UFC championship on Saturday does not move an inch in the ESPN divisional rankings. But several other fighters who did not even compete over the weekend do rise in their divisions' top 10s. One shifts from the top of one division's rankings to the middle of the pack in another weight class.

The new champion is Natalia Silva, who cruised past unranked Wang Cong at UFC 332 to capture the vacant women's flyweight title. Silva stays put at No. 2, however, below Valentina Shevchenko, who vacated the title while recovering from injury.

Several other weight classes saw significant shifts, in some cases because of a lack of fights and in one case because of a fight booking for the future.

The most significant move is Alex Pereira shifting into the heavyweight rankings following the UFC's announcement that he will face Sergei Pavlovich on Dec. 12. It will be the second straight heavyweight fight for the former middleweight and light heavyweight champion, who has been No. 1 in the 205-pound rankings. He now moves to the heavyweight top 10, where he is ranked No. 7, two spots behind Pavlovich.

At light heavyweight, everyone previously below Pereira moves up, with ex-champion Magomed Ankalaev now No. 1. New to the top 10 are ninth-ranked Bogdan Guskov and No. 10 Robert Whittaker, as Khalil Rountree Jr. is out because he has not fought in over a year.

Also ineligible because of inactivity is middleweight Nassourdine Imavov, who is replaced in the 185-pound rankings by Christian Leroy Duncan. Perfect timing, as Duncan fights No. 5 Brendan Allen on Saturday's UFC card.

The other top-10 newcomer is men's bantamweight Payton Talbott, who knocked out Deiveson Figueiredo at UFC 332 to oust him from the rankings.

Here are the ESPN pound-for-pound MMA rankings and a list of current UFC champions in all weight classes.

Results are current; rankings as of Oct. 6. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

stories.headline: New Zealand Rugby launches legal action against ARLC over 'Chiefs' name
stories.summary: The battle over the use of the "Chiefs" name is headed to the New Zealand High Court after New Zealand Rugby launched legal action against the Australian Rugby League Commission.
stories.body:
The battle over the use of the "Chiefs" name is headed to the New Zealand High Court after New Zealand Rugby launched legal action against the Australian Rugby League Commission.

NZR on Thursday said it had been left with no choice but to launch legal proceedings against the ARLC, who has sought to adopt the name for its Papua New Guinea expansion franchise.

The PNG Chiefs are due to join the NRL in 2028 and have already signed a raft of players, including code-hoppers Zac Lomaz and Joey Manu, but they may yet have to undergo a chanGe of name if NZR gets its way.

The Chiefs' Super Rugby franchise has existed since 1996, with NZR claiming the introduction of the PNG Chiefs would result in "significant confusion and damage" should they be allowed to compete under the name from 2028.

"New Zealand Rugby (NZR) has today moved to protect the Chiefs brand and is filing proceedings in the High Court of New Zealand against the decision by the Australian Rugby League Commission (ARLC) to launch a new NRL side using "Chiefs" in its name," an NZR statement read.  

"NZR is seeking both an interim and final injunction which stops the use of the names 'PNG Chiefs', 'Chiefs' or any other similar names in New Zealand.   

"The Chiefs have competed as a professional rugby team in Super Rugby since 1996 and over those 30 years, have built a strong identity and fanbase across New Zealand, Australia and internationally.  

"In New Zealand, NZR owns both the trademark rights for the word Chiefs and the Chiefs logo and since 1998, NZR has also held trademark protection for the Chiefs logo in Australia."

NZR claims it had tried to engage with the ARLC in an attempt to find a resolution, yet the commission was now intent on proceeding with the official launch of the PNG Chiefs on Oct. 21.

"For 30 years the Chiefs and their players have built an incredibly strong identity that is widely recognised and loved by fans," NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster said. "We have raised our concerns with the ARLC directly and consistently over the last year in attempting to find a resolution. We now have a responsibility to protect the Chiefs brand.   

"We want to be absolutely clear, this is not about rugby league's growth in the Pacific. We welcome the development of the Pacific region through sport and the passion that the people of Papua New Guinea have for both rugby and rugby league."  

The Chiefs won two Super Rugby titles in back-to-back seasons in 2012 and 2013, and were runners-up in Super Rugby Pacific this season after suffering a crushing defeat by the Hurricanes in the decider.

The Hamilton-based team has produced countless All Blacks since its inception, with Saturday's run-on team to face the Wallabies featuring six players from the franchise.

"Here in New Zealand, when people hear 'the Chiefs', they think of this club and this region. The identity carries significant cultural meaning and connection to the region and its people, we know it means a great deal to our players and coaches past and present, fans and supporters here and around the world," Chiefs CEO Simon Graafhuis said.   

"Teams in different sports and markets can exist alongside one another with the same name, but the issue here is the similarity of our sports competing in the same market, for the same fans, in overlapping windows."  

However, ARLC executive chairman Peter V'Landys later issued a stinging rebuke, insisting he would vigorously defend PNG's right to use the Chiefs as its team name.

"The hypocrisy is mind-blowing, considering the Auckland Blues in 1996 used the NSW Blues name without any consultation or approval. The NSW Blues had been the Blues for in excess of 50 years before that," he said.

"Rugby union is obviously feeling threatened by rugby league in New Zealand, with sell-outs at most rugby league games."

No date has yet been slated for the hearing in New Zealand's High Court.
